templates.why_chosen: A star before/after exemplar: panel (a) frameworks split the loop (red, on the CPU) from MatMul/Add/Relu kernels on the accelerator, panel (b) fuses both into colour-matched Loop-uTasks mapped onto L0/L1/L2 hardware tiers.
templates.what_to_learn: Keep the same operator colours (blue MatMul, yellow Relu, gray Add) in both panels so a reader tracks exactly which pieces move from the CPU-side loop into accelerator-resident tasks; note panel (b)'s extra L0/L1/L2 tiers cost effort to map back to (a).

templates.why_chosen: Mirrors the loop/schedule/hardware skeleton in both panels; red fill marks only the CPU-bound Loop box in (a), the one thing (b) fixes by folding it into uniform uTasks on the L0/L1/L2 grid.
templates.what_to_learn: Repeat the loop-plus-kernels skeleton in both panels, but colour only the anchor box that changes (the separate CPU Loop) so the eye finds the fix immediately; add a small legend mapping the multi-level L0/L1/L2 hardware boxes back to the simple CPU/accelerator split in (a), a step this figure skips.

templates.why_chosen: High-confidence pick where the floorplan payload sits only in panel (b): coloured uTasks map onto a nested L0-core, L1-SM and L2-device hardware hierarchy, contrasted against panel (a)'s plain CPU-driven loop and accelerator kernels.
templates.what_to_learn: When a hardware hierarchy is the point, draw it as boxes nested three levels deep with small coloured squares standing for identical tasks mapped onto each level, and pair it with a simpler baseline panel using the same colour key so a reader can trace exactly which piece moved onto the accelerator.
